mappings.name: collections token: minted for any subscription key the rail knows

metadata.why: The adapter mints one of these before every charge-path call it has no cached token for. `expires_in` is MTN's documented hour; the adapter refreshes a minute early.
metadata.why-the-matchers-are-this-strict: PR #177 fixed a real bug found against MTN's real sandbox: the grant must be the JSON spelling `{"grant_type":"client_credentials"}` with `Content-Type: application/json`, because MTN's gateway answers 411 to a bodyless POST and a 200 'Request Rejected' HTML page to the form-encoded spelling. This stub matched `{"contains": "client_credentials"}` until 2026-09-15, which the string `grant_type=client_credentials` ALSO satisfies — so the exact regression #177 fixed would have gone green here. `equalToJson` refuses a form body because a form body is not JSON, and the Content-Type matcher refuses it a second time. Proven by mutation: with the adapter's `.body(CLIENT_CREDENTIALS_JSON)` changed to `.form(..)`, `bad_credentials_are_not_reported_as_a_payer_problem` and every other wire case fail (see docs/status/verification/2026-09-15-mtn-disbursements-refund.md).

mappings.name: collections token: 'bad-key' is the subscription key the rail refuses

metadata.why: `bad_credentials_are_not_reported_as_a_payer_problem` in the conformance suite: credentials the rail rejects must surface as provider_account_blocked (severity Page), never as a decline. `bad-key` is the value that suite's `Credentials::Rejected` configures.
metadata.why-no-body-matcher: This one matches on the credential and not on the grant, deliberately: it is the higher-priority rule and it must fire for a bad key whatever the body is. The grant's spelling is enforced by the mapping above, which is the one that can answer 200.

mappings.name: disbursements token: minted for any subscription key the rail knows

metadata.why: MTN's Disbursements product is a separate subscription key, a separate token endpoint and a separately scoped token (docs/flows/adapter-mtn-momo.md, 'Credential hierarchy'). `mtn_momo::refund` mints from here and never from /collection/token/.
metadata.what-is-assumed: That the Disbursements token endpoint wants the same JSON grant and the same content type as Collections. NOBODY HAS CALLED IT — PR #177 measured Collections against MTN's real sandbox on 2026-09-15 and no call has ever been made to Disbursements from this repository. The matchers are the assumption written down, so that the day someone does call it a mismatch is visible here rather than inferred from a 200 'Request Rejected' page.
metadata.why-the-token-value-differs: `stub-disbursement-access-token` is a different string from the Collections stub's on purpose: transfer.json's 202 mapping matches the Authorization header against it, so an adapter that minted from /collection/token/ gets a 404 instead of a 202 (measured: 3 conformance cases fail). CORRECTED ON REVIEW, 2026-09-15 — this note named a test `a_refund_carries_a_disbursement_scoped_bearer` THAT DOES NOT EXIST AND NEVER DID; the case that drives the mapping is `a_refund_on_a_rail_that_refunds_reaches_the_rail_and_is_accepted`. It also claimed this was "the only way to prove the adapter did not serve a Collections bearer", which overstates it: see transfer.json's why-both-headers-are-matched note for what this suite can and cannot tell apart.
